tldr: Across 15 outlet buckets, headlines frame the FIFA crisis as a leadership-survival story — Infantino 'refuses to resign,' gets 'internal support,' or is declared 'to stay on' — while simultaneously naming the World Cup privatisation plan as the economic trigger. Canadian coverage foregrounds PM Carney's no-confidence declaration; French outlets emphasise the institutional apology and acknowledged errors.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Uses all-caps 'REFUSES to resign' — the only headline in the corpus to cast Infantino's continuation as wilful defiance rather than institutional endorsement or survival.

Uses the word 'curses' to describe Carney's statement — the only outlet to frame a political no-confidence declaration as a rhetorical assault, foregrounding state antagonism over institutional process.
Only headline in the corpus to allege a specific backroom deal: Infantino 'accusé d'avoir promis la finale du Mondial 2030 au Maroc' — a corruption-adjacent framing absent from all other outlets.

bottom_line: The headline layer advertises two parallel narratives: an institutional damage-control story (apology + full support for Infantino) and a political-survival story (REFUSES to resign / Carney declares no confidence), with the World Cup privatisation plan named in most titles as the triggering economic fact.
